news.title: Sports - FIFA President Gianni Infantino scraps controversial World Cup investment plan
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino was met with unprecedented backlash following his proposal for the structural reform of the World Cup. Under pressure, he announced that he was withdrawing his plan to sell part of the tournament to private investors. This proposal caused quite a stir internally and even led some members of his team to resign in protest.

news.title: FIFA scraps controversial $20 billion World Cup investment plan
news.lede: FIFA’s proposed plan to sell private stakes in upcoming World Cup tournaments that sparked backlash from fans and soccer associations around the world has been scrapped, FIFA president Gianni Infantino said in a statement Friday. “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place,” Infantino said. “Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. “As a result, this proposal will not proceed.”

news.title: 'Nobody is selling football!' - FIFA responds to controversy and offers explanation after Gianni Infantino's World Cup plan sparks outrage
news.lede: FIFA has issued a firm response to the mounting backlash surrounding its controversial World Cup spin-off proposal, insisting that "nobody is selling football." The governing body claims media reports mischaracterised the plans and reaffirmed its commitment to a democratic process. FIFA has officially responded to the fierce opposition surrounding its proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project. The governing body released a public statement attempting to clear up what it described as "incorrect media reports" that disrupted the planned consultation process.

news.title: Gianni Infantino abandons plans to sell off stakes in World Cup after widespread backlash
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has abandoned his controversial plan to sell a stake in future World Cup profits to private equity investors after fierce opposition from football's governing bodies. FIFA had announced on Tuesday that it was seeking to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would bring together the sale of FIFA's commercial rights - including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing - with the operational delivery of its tournaments. news.title: FIFA U-turn: Infantino drops plan to sell World Cup stakes
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has abandoned FIFA’s controversial plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors, a dramatic U-turn in the face of fierce opposition from national federations and clubs. The FIFA president confirmed in an official statement that the “FIFA Forward Enterprise” project, which would have created a commercial subsidiary to house the World Cup’s money-making arms and open the door to outside capital, will not proceed. “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that… are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place,” Infantino said, insisting his aim had always been “to unite and improve.” The reversal follows a ferocious backlash.
